summary: Dedicated tenant batching-tier override not taking effect (route policy appears to win over tenant override)
description:
Issue summary
- Dedicated customer reports that their tenant-level override for batching SLO tier (fast) is not being applied; effective behavior remains standard.
- Customer expectation (and internal design): customer override > route policy > tier default.
- Observed: route policy appears to override tenant setting (or tenant setting is ignored).

Customer impact
- Customer is attempting to force fast tier on a latency-sensitive streaming endpoint.
- They are seeing increased queueing and higher p99 compared to pre-tiered-defaults behavior.
- Impact limited to a subset of routes on their Dedicated cluster, but blocks their rollout of tiered defaults.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: northlake-dedicated-03
- Region: us-east
- Runtime train: 1.22.0 (feature flag enabled for tiered defaults)
- Control plane: 2026.04.08 build (policy evaluation service)

What the customer configured
1) Tenant override (Dedicated Console > Cluster > Runtime overrides): batching_tier=fast
2) Route policy (Console > Routes > /v1/chat/completions): batching_tier=standard (set earlier during testing)

Expected behavior
- Requests on that tenant/cluster should run fast tier regardless of route policy.

Actual behavior
- Requests continue to use standard tier.
- Telemetry shows selection_reason=route_policy for the affected route.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) In staging (or a dedicated test cluster), set tenant override batching_tier=fast at the cluster/tenant scope.
2) Set route policy batching_tier=standard on a specific route.
3) Send requests without request-level tier headers.
4) Observe effective tier via decision trace / metrics label.

Observed signals
- runtime.metric: redwood_inference_request_latency_ms{tier="standard",route="/v1/chat/completions"} increases.
- reason code emitted: profile_selection_reason="route_policy" even when tenant override is set.

Notes
- Customer also noted that toggling the tenant override off/on sometimes changes behavior after ~10 minutes, suggesting config propagation/cache involvement.

Requested outcome
- Fix precedence to match published behavior for Dedicated.
- Provide an immediate workaround + ETA for rollout to their cluster.
comments: 2026-04-10 09:14 PT - Rafael Mendes (Support): Customer report from Northlake: Dedicated tenant override set to fast tier but effective tier remains standard. They shared screenshots of Console showing override and route policy. Asking if this is expected precedence or a bug.
2026-04-10 09:33 PT - Henry Cho (PM, Hosted API): Precedence should be customer override > route policy > tier default per latest spec. If this is inverted, it’s a bug. Looping in Platform/Runtime.

2026-04-10 10:02 PT - Ethan Park (Assignee, Control plane): Acknowledged. We recently shipped tier policy evaluation changes behind the feature flag; could be a precedence ordering bug in the policy engine or a stale config cache in dedicated control plane.
Action: reproduce in staging with a route-tier set + tenant override set.

2026-04-10 12:21 PT - Jordan Lee (Policy engine): Repro’d in staging. Effective tier is standard when both are set. Decision trace shows evaluation order: (tier default) -> (tenant override) -> (route policy). Route policy applied last, overwriting tenant override. This is opposite of the intended precedence for Dedicated.

2026-04-10 12:49 PT - Lauren Bishop (PM, Dedicated): Confirmed requirement from Dedicated: tenant/cluster override must win. Route policy is for self-serve/hosted ergonomics; Dedicated customers treat tenant override as the authoritative contract. Please prioritize fix + comms for rollout.

2026-04-11 08:05 PT - Ethan Park: Root cause identified: policy-eval service uses a shared precedence table across Hosted and Dedicated. During implementation, we standardized order without an environment-specific override layer, so route policy was applied last universally.
Fix plan: introduce dedicated precedence mode: customer_override > route_policy > tier_default. Also ensure request-level header remains highest precedence when allowed.
Workaround: customer can remove route-level batching_tier setting to allow tenant override to apply (confirmed in staging).

2026-04-11 08:27 PT - Rafael Mendes (Support): Shared workaround with customer: remove route-level batching_tier or set it to inherit/default; tenant override will apply. Customer agrees as temporary mitigation but wants an ETA for fix and confirmation it won’t regress again.

2026-04-14 15:18 PT - Ethan Park: Fix is implemented and reviewed in runtime/control plane integration branch; aligning with Dedicated override precedence rules from ENG-18430. Will be shipped as part of runtime-1.22.1 + control plane hotfix. Tracking validation on one dedicated canary cluster.

2026-04-16 11:04 PT - Aisha Bello (SRE): Canary validation: precedence now correct; reason code emits profile_selection_reason="customer_override". No unexpected metric cardinality change observed. Suggest proceed with staged rollout to affected dedicated fleets.

2026-04-18 17:42 PT - Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): runtime-1.22.1 cut includes precedence fix; rollout starting with 2 dedicated canaries tonight. Control plane hotfix to policy-eval service goes out alongside. Kill switch available if route-policy behavior changes unexpectedly.

2026-04-20 09:08 PT - Rafael Mendes (Support): Customer confirmed in us-east after maintenance window that effective tier is now fast (selection reason shows customer_override) without removing their route policy. Latency returned to expected range. Requesting formal confirmation of fix details for their internal change log.

2026-04-21 10:22 PT - Ethan Park: Confirmed fix shipped. Summary sent to Support for customer: Dedicated precedence corrected; route policy no longer overwrites tenant override. Added regression test for precedence matrix. Closing ticket unless new reports arise.
resolution: Resolved by correcting tier override precedence in Dedicated mode: customer/tenant override now wins over route policy, which wins over tier default. Fix validated in staging and dedicated canary; shipped in runtime-1.22.1 with accompanying control plane policy-eval hotfix. Customer verified behavior in prod us-east. Temporary workaround (prior to rollout) was to remove route-level batching_tier to allow tenant override to apply.
attachments: Customer screenshots (Console override + route policy) attached in Jira (redacted).
Staging repro trace: decision_path shows route policy applied after tenant override (pre-fix).
